nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact connected Hausdorff spaces with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$. Every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$ has a degree, which is a natural number.
nodes.title: Degree of a holomorphic map

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface, that is, a compact connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$. The genus of $X$ is $0$ if and only if $X$ is homeomorphic to the unit sphere in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$.
nodes.title: A compact Riemann surface has genus zero iff it is a sphere

nodes.summary: For a compact Riemann surface $X$, that is, a compact connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$, the genus of $X$ is a natural number.
nodes.title: Genus of a compact Riemann surface

nodes.summary: For a compact Riemann surface $X$, that is, a compact connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$, the Jacobian $J(X)$ of $X$ is a type in the same universe as $X$.
nodes.title: Jacobian of a compact Riemann surface

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$, and let $J(X)$ be its Jacobian, a complex manifold modelled on $\mathbb{C}^g$. For every point $P \in X$, the Abel–Jacobi map $X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ is holomorphic.
nodes.title: The Abel–Jacobi map is holomorphic

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface with Jacobian $J(X)$, and let $P \in X$. If the genus of $X$ is positive, then the Abel–Jacobi map $X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ is injective.
nodes.title: The Abel–Jacobi map is injective in positive genus

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface with Jacobian $J(X)$, an abelian group. For every point $P \in X$, the Abel–Jacobi map $X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ sends $P$ to $0$.
nodes.title: The Abel–Jacobi map sends the base point to zero

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface with Jacobian $J(X)$. Each point $P \in X$ gives a map $X \to J(X)$, the Abel–Jacobi map based at $P$.
nodes.title: Abel–Jacobi map

nodes.summary: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be compact Riemann surfaces, and for a holomorphic map $h$ between compact Riemann surfaces write $h^*$ for the induced pullback map on Jacobians. For all holomorphic maps $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ and every point $P$ of the Jacobian $J(Z)$, we have $(g \circ f)^*(P) = f^*(g^*(P))$.
nodes.title: Pullback on Jacobians is compatible with composition

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces of genus $g_X$ and $g_Y$, with Jacobians $J(X)$ and $J(Y)$, complex manifolds modelled on $\mathbb{C}^{g_X}$ and $\mathbb{C}^{g_Y}$. For every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the induced pullback map $f^* : J(Y) \to J(X)$ is holomorphic.
nodes.title: The pullback map on Jacobians is holomorphic

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface, that is, a compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifold of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for its Jacobian. For every $P \in J(X)$, the pullback of $P$ along the identity map of $X$ is $P$: $(\mathrm{id}_X)^*(P) = P$.
nodes.title: Pullback along the identity

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for the Jacobian of $X$, an abelian group with a topology. For a holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the pullback $f^*$ is a continuous group homomorphism from $J(Y)$ to $J(X)$. It is meant to be the zero map when $f$ is constant and the usual pullback along $f$ otherwise; its…
nodes.title: Pullback on Jacobians

nodes.summary: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for the Jacobian of $X$. For all holomorphic maps $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ and every $P \in J(X)$, the pushforwards satisfy $(g \circ f)_*(P) = g_*(f_*(P))$.
nodes.title: Pushforward respects composition

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, of genera $g_X$ and $g_Y$. The Jacobian $J(X)$ of $X$ is a complex-analytic manifold modeled on $\mathbb{C}^{g_X}$, and likewise $J(Y)$ on $\mathbb{C}^{g_Y}$. For every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the pushforward $f_* : J(X) \to J(Y)$ is holomorphic.
nodes.title: The pushforward on Jacobians is holomorphic

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface, that is, a compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifold of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for its Jacobian. For every $P \in J(X)$, the pushforward of $P$ along the identity map of $X$ is $P$: $(\mathrm{id}_X)_*(P) = P$.
nodes.title: Pushforward along the identity

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(Y)$ for the Jacobian of $Y$, an abelian group. For every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$ and every $P \in J(Y)$, the pushforward along $f$ of the pullback of $P$ along $f$ is $\deg(f) \cdot P$, where the degree $\deg(f)$ is a natural number: $f_*(f^*(P)) = \deg(f) \cdot P$.
nodes.title: Pushforward of a pullback is multiplication by the degree

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for the Jacobian of $X$, an abelian group with a topology. For a holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the pushforward $f_*$ is a continuous group homomorphism from $J(X)$ to $J(Y)$. It is meant to be the homomorphism induced by $f$; its properties are stated separately.
nodes.title: Pushforward on Jacobians

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
